body.statement: Assuming \(\mathcal M_{T_0,T_1}(0)\ne\varnothing\), use \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{or}}(\gamma;T_0,T_1)\) to construct an evaluable profile \(\Phi_{\mathrm{or}}(\gamma;T_0,T_1)\) and a \(\gamma\)-aware confidence set, and prove \(R_{\mathrm{or}}(\gamma)\asymp\Phi_{\mathrm{or}}(\gamma;T_0,T_1)\) at the same sample sizes for every nonempty stratum. The characterization must cover disconnected near-maximal loading geometries, all finite component-classification transitions, unequal \(T_0,T_1\), zero margin, small effects, and \(A\)- and \(B\)-saturation, with lower bounds evaluated under the original full observations rather than a noiseless-label reduction.
body.justification: This is the load-bearing open content: constant-rescaled pairwise moduli do not determine risk across disconnected component thresholds.
body.gap: CaiLow2004 treats ordered moduli for linear functionals and EvansHansenStark2005 treats restricted-location confidence decisions; neither evaluates the sparse-compatible, estimated-subspace component experiment generated here.
body.consumer: Its solution determines when a supplied geometry certificate materially shortens full-vector intervals and makes the oracle benchmark operational.

obligation.what_is_open: A same-sample constant-factor characterization of the oracle expected-diameter frontier on every nonempty margin stratum, including all disconnected-component classification transitions.
obligation.obstruction: The explicit sparse-compatible modulus is nonconvex and can jump when its loading-projector radius first reaches a second connected component.  The proved upper and lower bounds evaluate that modulus at different constant multiples of the pre- and post-resolution radii.  No uniform doubling, concavity, or component-testing identity follows from the frozen primitives, so replacing those two radii by one would be an unsupported step, especially near maximal-margin geometries.
obligation.attempted: Restricted the support-enumerated confidence inversion to the margin stratum for the upper bound; lifted arbitrary modulus pairs to Procrustes-aligned loading frames with exact normalized pre factors and constant post factors for the original-data Gaussian lower bound; proved the weak-margin rotation regime and the four-line maximal endpoint separately.  A bounded \(N=8,r=2,s=3\) search recovered the harmonic-frame candidate margin \(0.1379496896\) but produced no analytic maximality or component certificate, so it cannot certify a finite component rule.  Extending the rotation argument to intermediate high margins loses stratum membership, while treating separated components by a generic testing error does not yield the exact expected-diameter transition.
obligation.partial_result:
Let \(\mathcal G_\gamma=\{L'\in\operatorname{Gr}(r,N):\kappa_s(L')\ge\gamma\}\).  For \(x_0,x_1\ge0\), the strongest proved computable comparison is the compact sparse-compatible modulus
\[
\Omega_\gamma(x_0,x_1)=\sup\lVert b-b'\rVert_2,
\]
where the supremum is over \(L,L'\in\mathcal G_\gamma\), their projectors satisfying \(\lVert P_L-P_{L'}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\le x_0\), vectors \(m\in L\), \(m'\in L'\) with \(\lVert m\rVert_2,\lVert m'\rVert_2\le A\), and \(s\)-sparse \(b,b'\in[-B,B]^N\) satisfying \(\lVert(m+b)-(m'+b')\rVert_2\le x_1\).  Support enumeration makes this a finite union of compact semialgebraic optimizations.  Restricting the global feasibility set to \(\mathcal G_\gamma\) gives the same-sample upper bound
\[
R_{\mathrm{or}}(\gamma)\le
\Omega_\gamma(2\delta_0,2\varepsilon_1).
\]
Conversely, for fixed-class constants \(c,c_0,c_1>0\), Procrustes-aligned loading frames, a common admissible \(D,F,\sigma\), constant post factors, and the two-point confidence-set inequality give
\[
R_{\mathrm{or}}(\gamma)\ge
c\,\Omega_\gamma(c_0T_0^{-1/2},c_1T_1^{-1/2}).
\]
Indeed, a feasible pair at these radii has full pre squared mean distance at most \(2rT_0d_{\mathrm{hi}}^2x_0^2\) and full post squared mean distance at most \(T_1x_1^2\), so its total-variation distance is bounded away from \(1-2\alpha\).  This proves an explicit original-observation modulus sandwich, but not the requested equivalence at one common resolution.
